name: overnight_v0
hypothesis: US equity index returns accrue mainly outside regular cash-market hours. Cliff, Cooper and Gulen (2008) find that night returns are strongly positive and day returns close to zero, and say the effect holds for individual stocks, equity indexes and futures contracts on equity indexes on both NYSE and Nasdaq. Kelly and Clark (2011) report a QQQ close-to-open premium of +23.7%/yr against an open-to-close premium of -23.3%/yr for 1999-2006. Boyarchenko, Larsen and Whelan (2023) find that almost all of the premium in E-mini S&P futures is earned between 02:00 and 03:00 ET, which lies inside the close-to-open window. Bondarenko and Muravyev (2023) find that 4 hours around the European open account for the whole E-mini S&P return. H1, fixed before any NQ result is seen: holding one NQ contract long from the NYSE cash close to the next NYSE session's 09:30 ET open, and flat during the day, earns a positive mean NET P&L per trade after 1 tick of slippage per side and $2.24/side fees. The prior is honestly mixed. Knuteson (2020) says the overnight/intraday divergence in the S&P 500 and NASDAQ Composite stopped after 2008, which is exactly our 2010-2021 sample. Lou, Polk and Skouras find the CRSP value-weighted premium split roughly 60/40 overnight/intraday for 1993-2013, although for the largest stocks essentially all of it came overnight. The New York Fed authors report the drift disappeared only from 2021 onward.
rule:
DATA: bars = nq_lab.data.serve(pd.Timestamp('2010-09-28', tz='UTC'), pd.Timestamp('2022-01-01', tz='UTC'), caller='overnight_v0', reason='pre-registered overnight vs intraday test, in-sample only', variant='repaired'). Make this one call and never set end > 2022-01-01 UTC. Column ts is the bar OPEN in UTC, so the bar with ts=T covers [T, T+1min). Sessions: S = nq_lab.sessions.nyse_sessions(date(2010,9,28), date(2021,12,31)), which is XNYS from exchange_calendars and includes holidays, unscheduled closures (such as Hurricane Sandy 2012-10-29/30 and 2018-12-05) and 13:00 ET early closes.

DST: never hard-code UTC clock times. Every time is derived from S.open_utc and S.close_utc, which exchange_calendars builds in America/New_York and converts to UTC. The ET open is always 09:30 and the ET close is 16:00, or 13:00 on early_close days. Nights that span a DST switch are simply one hour longer or shorter; no adjustment is made.

ENTRY (overnight leg): for session s_k, the entry bar is the bar with ts == close_utc(s_k) - 1 minute. That is the 15:59 ET bar, or the 12:59 ET bar on early closes. The entry price is that bar's c, which is the price at ~16:00:00 ET. Fallback: the c of the last bar with ts in [close_utc-5min, close_utc). If there is none, skip the night and log reason 'no entry bar'.

EXIT: s_{k+1} is the NEXT row of S, whatever the calendar gap. The exit bar is the bar with ts == open_utc(s_{k+1}), the 09:30 ET bar, and the exit price is its o. Fallback: the o of the first bar with ts in (open_utc, open_utc+5min]. If there is none, use the o of the first bar with ts > open_utc before close_utc(s_{k+1}) and flag the night 'late_exit'. The night is not dropped, so limit-locked or halted opens are not survivorship-filtered out. If the exit session has no bar at all, drop the night and log 'no exit bar'.

WEEKENDS AND HOLIDAYS: hold straight through. Friday close to Monday open, and pre-holiday close to post-holiday open, each count as ONE trade. This follows Lou-Polk-Skouras, who define overnight so that (1+overnight)(1+intraday) = close-to-close and hold from the close of s-1 to the next available open.

DIRECTION: long only, 1 NQ contract. Flat from each session's open to its close.

TRADE: exactly one round trip per consecutive NYSE session pair (s_k, s_{k+1}) with s_k >= 2010-09-28 and s_{k+1} <= 2021-12-31. The last trade enters at the 2021-12-30 close and exits at the 2021-12-31 open. The 2021-12-31 close to 2022-01-03 open night is SEALED and is never computed.

P&L: gross_pts = exit - entry on the back-adjusted series, which is additive, so the point difference is valid across a roll. Net cost is applied as fixed points. NQ: per side 0.25 pt slippage + $2.24/$20 = 0.112 pt, so 0.362 pt/side and 0.724 pt ($14.48) per round trip. At 2 ticks: 0.612/side, 1.224 pt ($24.48) per round trip. MNQ ($2/pt): per side 0.25 + $0.61/$2 = 0.555 pt, so 1.11 MNQ-pts ($2.22) per round trip; at 2 ticks 1.61 pt ($3.22). Break-even gross is 0.724 pt on NQ and 1.11 pt on MNQ.

BLOCK: each trade is assigned by its ENTRY session date: 2010-09-28..2013-12-31, 2014-01-01..2017-12-31, 2018-01-01..2021-12-30.

INTRADAY COMPARISON LEG (same bar rules): long at the o of the ts==open_utc(s) bar, exit at the c of the ts==close_utc(s)-1min bar in the same session, same costs, sessions 2010-09-28..2021-12-31.

IDENTITY CHECK: for every session d, overnight_gross(d-1->d) + intraday_gross(d) must equal c(close bar d) - c(close bar d-1) exactly. Write this guard so it is born failing first, for example by shifting the exit bar by 1 minute.

NO day_gate FILTER on the headline. Validity is bar existence only, as above. Report a day_gate-on-both-sessions variant as a sensitivity only.
comparisons: HEADLINE: overnight long, mean NET points per trade (NQ, 1 tick/side + $2.24/side) with per-trade t = mean/(sd/sqrt(n)). Also report n, dollars per trade, hit rate, and annualised Sharpe from nq_lab.metrics.sharpe on the daily P&L series, plus max_drawdown.

Complementary INTRADAY leg (09:30 open to 16:00 close or 13:00 on early closes, long, same costs): mean net points and t. Also report the paired per-session difference overnight_gross - intraday_gross with its t. This is the literature's own test and is not gating.

BUY-AND-HOLD BASELINE over the same clocks: gross (zero-cost) close-to-close points per session, which equals the sum of the two legs by the identity check. Report the fraction of total B&H points earned overnight versus intraday. Report the B&H annualised Sharpe against the overnight-net Sharpe. Report the gross overnight mean as the zero-cost version of the headline.

Cost ladder: gross (0 ticks, no fees), 1 tick (headline) and 2 ticks per side, for both NQ and MNQ economics (MNQ costs 1.11 pt per round trip at 1 tick against NQ's 0.724, so it needs a larger point edge). MNQ was only listed from 2019 (UNVERIFIED), so MNQ figures before then are hypothetical.
Three blocks by entry date: 2010-13, 2014-17, 2018-21. Mean net, t and n in each.

Subsets (descriptive, not gating): weeknight nights (next session is the next calendar day) versus weekend/holiday nights (gap > 1 day); early-close entry nights; roll nights (instrument_id of the entry bar differs from the exit bar) versus non-roll nights; 'late_exit' flagged nights; long-gap nights (gap > 4 calendar days, e.g. Sandy).

Scale robustness (descriptive): per-trade return in bp = gross_pts / raw_c at the entry bar, with its t, because NQ's price level rose several-fold over 2010-2021, so a points metric overweights late years.

Descriptive-only split of the overnight gross into sub-windows 16:00-18:00, 18:00-02:00, 02:00-03:00 (the Boyarchenko-Larsen-Whelan window) and 03:00-09:30 ET, using close-of-bar prices at those ET times from tz-converted ts. Not gating and not a new hypothesis.
Serial-correlation robustness: Newey-West (5 lags) t alongside the iid per-trade t.
Bonferroni across the 3 calendar/event hypotheses: report p_adj = min(1, 3*p_one_sided) for the headline, separately from the pass bar.
pass_bar: PASS only if ALL of the following hold on the headline (overnight long, NQ, 1 tick/side + $2.24/side): (1) per-trade t of mean net points >= 2.5; (2) mean net points per trade > 0 in each of the 2010-13, 2014-17 and 2018-21 blocks (by entry date), i.e. the same sign as the full sample; (3) mean net points per trade >= 0 at 2 ticks/side slippage (1.224 pt round trip). The Bonferroni-adjusted p across the 3 hypotheses is reported separately and does not change PASS/FAIL. Everything else (intraday leg, overnight-minus-intraday difference, sub-windows, subsets, the bp version, MNQ) is descriptive and cannot rescue a FAIL. No parameter (entry/exit time, weekend treatment, fallbacks, cost) may change after the first result is computed. A variant must be registered as overnight_v1 with a new spec hash.
pitfalls: Timestamp alignment: ts is the bar OPEN. The 16:00 close price is the c of the bar with ts = close_utc - 1min (15:59 ET), not the ts=16:00 bar, which holds post-close Globex trading. The 09:30 open price is the o of the ts = open_utc bar; using its c would silently move the exit 1 minute later.
DST: derive every time from nyse_sessions open_utc/close_utc. Hard-coding 14:30/21:00 UTC is wrong for about 8 months of every year.

Sealed window: the 2021-12-31 close to 2022-01-03 open night must never be formed. The serve() end must be <= 2022-01-01 UTC; the OOS gate refuses straddling windows rather than clipping them. Do not extend the read to 'finish' the last night.

Look-ahead and selection bias: do not drop nights with qa.day_gate on the EXIT session, and do not filter on price outcomes. The gate's RTH bar-count test correlates with halts and limit-locked opens (e.g. March 2020), so removing those days biases a long strategy upward. Use bar existence plus a flagged late-exit fallback, and report how many nights were skipped and why.

Unrepairable days (nq-lab project rules): 6 days in 2014 with no trades on the server, 4 March 2020 limit/halt days, and 2010-09-28 (server error). Nights touching them are skipped by the bar-existence rule or take a late exit; list them explicitly.

Repaired bars: rebuilt 2010-2015 days can differ from vendor bars by 1-2 ticks at minute boundaries (nq-lab project rules), which adds noise to 09:30 open and 15:59 close prices on repaired days. Report the result with repaired days excluded as a sensitivity.

Roll nights: the back-adjusted series is additive, so point P&L across a roll is right in principle. But the nq-lab project rules record that older roll gaps differ by 0.25-2 pts between products, which nudges overnight returns on roll nights, and a real trader would exit the entry contract (the instrument_id at the entry bar) at 09:30 rather than the new front month. Flag roll nights and report results with them excluded.

Weekends and holidays: holding Friday to Monday carries about 3 days of carry and weekend gap risk in one trade, and futures excess returns are below spot by (r - q) per calendar day. Report weeknight and weekend nights separately. Unscheduled NYSE closures (Sandy 2012) create multi-day 'nights'.

Early closes: entry is the 12:59 ET bar close on 13:00 early-close days, never 15:59. CME equity futures stop early on those days (exact CME halt time UNVERIFIED), so any bar at 15:59 would not exist or would be meaningless.

CME schedule changes: a 15:15-15:30 CT (16:15-16:30 ET) Globex halt existed until 2021-06-28. It falls outside both legs and has no effect, but the builder must not use any bar in 16:15-16:30 ET as an entry fallback.

The literature's 'open' differs from ours: Cliff-Cooper-Gulen say part of the effect comes from high opening prints that fall back in the first hour, and Lou-Polk-Skouras use the 09:30-10:00 VWAP as the open. Our exit is the tradable futures price at 09:30:00, which is the right choice for a real strategy but may capture less of the published effect.

Scale drift: costs are fixed in points but NQ's price level grew several-fold, so relative cost falls across the sample and point P&L variance rises. The points t-stat is dominated by 2018-21. That is why the block test and the bp-return version exist.

Cost sensitivity: two fills per night (0.724 NQ pt at 1 tick) must be charged on every one of roughly 2,800 nights. A small gross edge (a few points/night on a ~50 pt nightly SD, UNVERIFIED rough prior) makes the result highly sensitive to slippage, so the 2-tick stress is binding. Measured fills in results/quote_check_v1.json were +0.72 tick at entry and +1.0 at close, taken at other times of day.

Publication decay and regime: Knuteson says the US index divergence stopped around 2008; the New York Fed authors say the drift vanished in 2021-2025. A pass concentrated in one block would fail criterion (2).
Multiple testing: this is 1 of 3 pre-registered calendar hypotheses. The descriptive sub-windows and subsets must not be promoted to headline after the fact.
evidence: Cliff, Cooper and Gulen (2008), 'Return Differences between Trading and Non-Trading Hours: Like Night and Day', SSRN 1004081, DOI 10.2139/ssrn.1004081 (https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=1004081, found via OpenAlex at https://api.openalex.org/works?search=like%20night%20and%20day%20return%20differences%20trading%20non-trading%20hours). The abstract as returned in a search snippet says the US equity premium over the last decade is solely due to overnight returns: night returns strongly positive, day returns close to zero and sometimes negative. For S&P 500 stocks over 1993-2006, night returns average 2.82-4.76 bp and day returns -2.85 to 0.22 bp. The effect holds for stocks, equity indexes and futures on equity indexes across NYSE and Nasdaq, and is driven partly by high opening prices that decline in the first hour. The full text could not be fetched: SSRN and the super.so PDF returned 403.

Kelly and Clark (2011), 'Returns in trading versus non-trading hours: The difference is day and night', Journal of Asset Management 12(2):132-145 (abstract at https://econpapers.repec.org/article/palassmgt/v_3a12_3ay_3a2011_3ai_3a2_3ad_3a10.1057_5fjam.2011.2.htm). They use broad index ETFs and Sharpe ratios. From a search snippet of https://link.springer.com/article/10.1057/jam.2011.2: QQQQ 1999-2006 geometric close-to-open premium +23.7%/yr against open-to-close -23.3%/yr, with lower overnight volatility.

Lou, Polk and Skouras (2019), 'A tug of war: Overnight versus intraday expected returns', JFE 134(1):192-213 (https://personal.lse.ac.uk/polk/research/TugOfWar.pdf, read pp.195-199). Intraday return = close/open - 1, where open is the 09:30-10:00 VWAP; overnight return = (1+close-to-close)/(1+intraday) - 1. If the open is missing they hold from the close of s-1 to the next available open, so weekends are inside the overnight return. Sample is CRSP 1993-2013. The CRSP value-weighted market has monthly excess return 0.43%, split into intraday 0.38% and overnight 0.55%. They say the premium is not purely overnight except for the largest stocks, where essentially all of it is earned overnight.

Boyarchenko, Larsen and Whelan (2023), 'The Overnight Drift', RFS 36(9):3502-3547 (https://academic.oup.com/rfs/article-abstract/36/9/3502/7076616). E-mini S&P 500 futures: almost 100% of the US equity premium is earned between 02:00 and 03:00 ET, and the drift is related to order imbalances at the previous US close.

Boyarchenko, Larsen and Whelan, 'The Disappearing Overnight Drift', Liberty Street Economics, 1 July 2026 (https://libertystreeteconomics.newyorkfed.org/2026/07/the-disappearing-overnight-drift/). The original sample was 1998-2020, with confirmatory analysis on E-mini Nasdaq-100 (NQ) and Dow futures. The 02:00-03:00 window earned about 3.7%/yr but 'has averaged close to zero since 2021', which they link to the dispersion of closing order imbalances falling from 6.5% to 2.9%.

Bondarenko and Muravyev (2023), 'Market Return Around the Clock: A Puzzle', JFQA 58(3):939-967 (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-financial-and-quantitative-analysis/article/abs/market-return-around-the-clock-a-puzzle/089E33AC0B4D3B9A02CBA31EDF6505B3). E-mini S&P 500: 4 hours around the European open account for the entire average market return, with Sharpe 1.6 that stays high after costs. The other 20 hours average a noisy zero.

Knuteson (2020), 'Strikingly Suspicious Overnight and Intraday Returns', arXiv 2010.01727 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2010.01727). Fig. 1 plots cumulative overnight and intraday returns for the SPY and NASDAQ Composite from 1990 to 2020. Footnote 17 says that before 2008 the overnight and intraday returns of the S&P 500 and NASDAQ Composite diverged, and that since 2008 there has been no such divergence. This is a non-peer-reviewed source.

Lachance, 'Night trading: Lower risk but higher returns?', Review of Financial Economics 2023 (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/rfe.1180; SSRN 2633476). Overnight biases are persistent across stocks, and implementation costs are discussed. Summary from a search snippet only.

Elm Wealth, 'Night Moves' (https://elmwealth.com/night-moves-overnight-drift/). Uses SPY and S&P 500 stocks over 1995-2022. It says the effect weakened over the last decade and that a trader paying even 1 bp per trade would not have made money in the last 8 years on the long-short version. This is practitioner evidence.
CME removed the 15:15-15:30 CT Globex halt for equity index futures on 2021-06-28 (https://www.ampfutures.com/news/cme-equity-index-products-trading-halt-between-315-and-330-pm-removed).

Project facts: in-sample window, serve() and variant='repaired', unrepairable days, roll-gap discrepancies, and measured fill slippage, all from the nq-lab project rules. XNYS sessions with early_close come from src/nq_lab/sessions.py. The OOS gate refuses straddling windows (src/nq_lab/oos_gate.py).
unverified: Cliff-Cooper-Gulen's exact treatment of weekends/holidays in 'night' returns, and which index futures and times they used. The full text was blocked (SSRN/super.so 403), and the numbers come only from the abstract via a search snippet.
Kelly-Clark's QQQQ numbers (+23.7% / -23.3%) and their weekend treatment come from a search-result snippet; the Springer page redirected to a login.
Whether the Boyarchenko-Larsen-Whelan NQ confirmatory result covers 2010-2021 specifically. The blog only gives the 1998-2020 sample and gives no NQ numbers.
The Bondarenko-Muravyev sample period, and whether E-mini close-to-open (16:00->09:30) is positive in 2010-2021.
NQ daily settlement time over the whole sample (currently 15:00 CT = 16:00 ET is believed; the search result found this only for the E-mini NASDAQ Composite), and any change during 2010-2012.
CME equity futures early-close halt time on NYSE 13:00 early-close days (believed 12:15 CT / 13:15 ET).
MNQ listing date (believed 2019-05-06), so MNQ economics before then are hypothetical.
Whether NQ traded (and at what price) at 09:30 on the March 2020 limit-down mornings. The late-exit fallback handles either case.
The rough prior of a few points of gross edge per night against a ~50 pt nightly SD is my back-of-envelope from public index levels, not from project data.
Globex behaviour around unscheduled NYSE closures (Sandy 2012-10-29/30) and Good Friday NFP sessions. Neither affects the rule, since positions are simply held to the next NYSE open.
builder_resolutions: C1 (all specs) Bonferroni family: the specs say 3 hypotheses, but this run freezes and tests 4 specs (tom_v0, preholiday_v0, prefomc_v0, overnight_v0). The screen reports the pre-registered p x 3 AND p x 4 (the number actually tested); neither changes any pass bar. p is one-sided (H1: mean > 0) from Student t with n-1 df.

C2 (all specs) Roll extra round trip, where a spec charges one, is charged at the same cost level as the scenario it is added to (0.724 pts at NQ 1 tick, 1.224 at NQ 2 ticks, 1.11/1.61 for MNQ, 0 in the zero-cost gross line).

C3 (all specs) raw_c for the % / bp return: rows rebuilt by scripts/repair_broken_days.py may carry no raw_c. When raw_c is missing on the entry bar, use c - offset_id, where offset_id is the median of (c - raw_c) over rows of the same instrument_id that do have raw_c in the served frame. Only descriptive % / bp numbers use it.

C4 (all specs) Repaired days = dates with a file in data/processed/repairs/ that are not listed under 'skipped' in results/repair_report.json. Unrepairable days = the 'skipped' dates in results/repair_report.json plus 2010-09-28.

C5 (all specs) One serve() call per spec over [2010-09-28, 2022-01-01) UTC with the spec's caller and reason and variant='repaired'. Everything else is computed from that frame; nothing reads 2022 or later.
C6 (all specs) Placebo draws use numpy default_rng(seed=20260926).

O1 Sharpe and max_drawdown come from nq_lab.metrics on a daily USD series: each night's NQ net USD is booked on its exit session date, reindexed over every realised session in the sample with zeros. The B&H Sharpe uses the zero-cost close-to-close USD per session on the same index.

O2 Sub-window split (descriptive): the price at ET clock t is the c of the last bar with entry_ts < ts < t; boundaries are 18:00 ET on the calendar day before the exit date, then 02:00 and 03:00 ET on the exit date; the last segment ends at the exit price. When no bar exists in a segment the previous boundary price is carried. Segments telescope to the gross.

O3 Identity check: for session d with an overnight night (d-1 -> d) whose exit bar is the intraday leg's entry bar and both close bars exist, overnight_gross + intraday_gross must equal c(close d) - c(close d-1) within 1e-9 (prices are exact binary multiples of 0.25). The guard is born failing in tests with the exit bar shifted by one minute.

O4 The intraday leg uses the same fallbacks: entry o at the ts == open_utc bar, else the first bar in (open_utc, open_utc + 5 min], else the first bar before close_utc (flagged late); exit c at the close bar with the [close - 5 min, close) fallback. A session with neither is skipped and logged.
O5 day_gate sensitivity: nights kept only when qa.day_gate passes on the RTH bars [open_utc, close_utc) of both the entry and the exit session.
O6 Newey-West t uses Bartlett weights with 5 lags on the net-point series in trade order.
O7 Entry fallback never reaches into 16:15-16:30 ET: the fallback window is [close_utc - 5 min, close_utc), which is always before the close.
